landing.metadataDescription: Build a structured role manual for hiring, onboarding, and team review.
landing.heroTitle: A role guide your team will use
landing.heroSubtitle: Build more than a formal template: AI turns your company context into 26 useful sections for hiring, onboarding, and managing the role.
landing.heroMethodologyLine: Built from practices used by Netflix, Amazon, Toyota, Spotify, Bridgewater, and Google.
landing.heroBooksLine: Expanded with ideas from Topgrading, Who, Drive, The Alliance, and The Checklist Manifesto.
landing.heroPreviewTitle: A role guide people can actually use
landing.heroPreviewSubtitle: A document people keep using after hiring: for onboarding, managing the role, and checking expectations quickly.
landing.heroPreviewQualityText: Not a half-page job post, but an editable guide with ownership, decisions, metrics, workflows, and growth context that a team can keep using after day one.
landing.personalizationTitle: Not a template, a guide for your company
landing.personalizationDescription: The constructor accounts for team size, product stage, department, role level, reporting line, and output language. The result feels like a working company document, not a universal sample.

0.title: Company context
0.description: Capture where the role works: department, team size, product stage, reporting line, and language.

1.title: AI assembles the structure
1.description: The system maps answers to 26 sections and management sources to create a coherent draft.

2.title: You keep control

landing.methodologyTitle: Built from operating systems used by serious teams
landing.methodologySubtitle: These are the six sources we use most often. Each source maps to concrete sections of the Role Guide, so the output explains purpose, autonomy, routines, quality bars, and collaboration boundaries.
landing.selectedBlocksLabel: Where the selected source is used
landing.selectedBlocksDescription: Click a source on the right: these are the instruction sections it helps shape.

netflix.title: Netflix Context over Control
netflix.description: Gives the role strategic context, clear boundaries, and room to act without micromanagement.

amazon.title: Amazon Leadership Principles
amazon.description: Turns culture into decision rules, input metrics, counter-metrics, and customer-oriented judgment.

toyota.title: Toyota Standardized Work
toyota.description: Captures the best-known way of working through checklists, exceptions, and quality criteria.

spotify.title: Spotify Squad Model
spotify.description: Shows how the role fits into real work streams, dependencies, squads, and growth paths.

bridgewater.title: Bridgewater Baseball Cards
bridgewater.description: Documents strengths, communication style, energy patterns, risks, and candidate fit.

google.title: Google Team Effectiveness
google.description: Helps describe the conditions where a role performs best: clear expectations, dependencies, collaboration, and review cadence.

examples.block1: The role turns B2B pipeline into predictable revenue: it qualifies opportunities, moves deals forward, and keeps the funnel healthy.
examples.block2: The B2B sales manager does not own post-launch support, approve unusual legal terms, or act as the product owner.
examples.block3: The role owns opportunity qualification, deal progress, forecast accuracy, and expectation handoff to implementation teams.
examples.block4: Update the pipeline weekly, run customer meetings, capture next steps, and prepare commercial proposals.
examples.block5: Small discounts can move quickly; larger discounts and unusual contract terms require commercial approval.
examples.block6: Qualified pipeline, win rate, sales cycle, and first-year retention are paired to prevent metric gaming.
examples.block7: A strong candidate can negotiate, understand customer economics, capture commitments, and handle long sales cycles calmly.
examples.block8: CRM, calendar, proposal templates, meeting notes, and an objection library work as one operating system.
examples.block9: Digital tools help draft follow-ups and meeting summaries, while the person confirms the final customer promise.
examples.block10: The role depends on marketing, product, legal, and implementation; slow answers from these teams slow the deal.
examples.block11: Growth moves from owning standard deals to strategic negotiations and coaching junior sales managers.
examples.block12: The profile needs complex-sales experience, structure, CRM discipline, strong questions, and tolerance for ambiguity.
examples.block13: The day starts with pipeline and next-step review, then customer meetings, commitment capture, and proposal work.
examples.block14: First 30 days cover product, market, and CRM; by day 60 the person owns deals; by day 90 they own forecast rhythm.
examples.block15: The role is motivated by a clear target, an honest pipeline, negotiation autonomy, and visible revenue impact.
examples.block16: Every deal has a next step, date, owner, and success criterion; exceptions are captured separately.
examples.block17: Red flags: promises without confirmation, empty CRM, discount-first selling, and no next step after a meeting.
examples.block18: If a customer asks for unusual terms, the manager captures the business reason and escalates for commercial approval.
examples.block19: Enterprise sales require trust, forecast accuracy, and understanding how the customer buys internally.
examples.block20: The business goal is to increase predictable revenue and reduce leakage at key funnel stages.
examples.block21: When pipeline weakens, the role checks lead quality, response speed, loss reasons, and next-step discipline.
examples.block22: The role memo captures mission, key decisions, ownership areas, and collaboration rules with other teams.
examples.block23: A handoff preserves deal status, key contacts, risks, commitments, and the next actions.
examples.block24: The role canvas shows customers, internal teams, influence points, decision zones, and main dependencies.
examples.block25: Every quarter, the manager and employee review metrics, role boundaries, workflows, and next-period expectations.
examples.block26: Before launching the role, check the owner, goals, metrics, tools, meeting rhythm, access, and first-90-days plan.

antiGoals.excerpt: The B2B sales manager does not own post-launch support, approve unusual legal terms, or act as the product owner.

landing.faqTitle: What to know before the first draft
landing.faqDescription: A short practical check: who should use the constructor, whether the result can be refined, and what to prepare before starting.

0.question: Who should use this first?
0.answer: HR leaders, founders, department heads, and enablement teams that need role clarity before hiring, onboarding, or training.

1.question: Can the generated guide be refined?
1.answer: Yes. The current version supports block-level review and refinement, so a team can tighten specific sections without restarting discovery.

2.question: What should I prepare before starting?
2.answer: A job description, role notes, team context, or a rough list of responsibilities is enough. The constructor asks follow-up questions where context is thin.
